title: Eyleme — Open-source Ecosystem & Specialist Subscriptions
description: Eyleme is an open-source ecosystem in development. Explore Derleme for field data and Onama for cybersecurity and governance, with paid specialist subscriptions.
headline: From intent
to action.
Together.
intro: Eyleme aims to grow into an open-source AI ecosystem shaped by its community. Its local task tool is the starting point; Derleme brings field data into the picture, and Onama addresses security, authority and responsibility.
status: In development. The local task foundation exists; the wider ecosystem and commercial services are still being built. First-party core code and docs: Apache-2.0.

principles.title: Open-source ecosystem
principles.text: Grow Eyleme through shared code, knowledge, examples and reviewed contributions. The community is part of the product’s future.

principles.title: Connected to the physical world
principles.text: Derleme is being built to collect field data and record it in the cloud or on premises. Onama addresses how that data and related actions are governed.

principles.title: Specialist subscriptions
principles.text: Derleme and Onama are paid products in development, focused on data infrastructure, cybersecurity and governance expertise.

architecture_intro: The open-source Eyleme tool owns its local authority, execution and evidence. Architecture v0.7 connects optional model roles with typed tools, skills, source-grounded retrieval and purpose-scoped memory.
technology_alt: Eyleme architecture v0.7: human goals and five separate data-use permissions govern jobs, nine optional model roles, tools and skills, Rust authority and observed feedback. Permitted sources supply RAG/recall context with six optional memory kinds and renewed rights, lineage and expiry checks. A separate planned loop moves permitted episodes through curation, native Rust LoRA/QLoRA training, held-out evaluation and human-controlled promotion back to model profiles and skills. Scoped implemented components are labeled separately; integrated retrieval and training still require acceptance.
technology_caption: Architecture v0.7 integration design. Nine optional roles use source-gated knowledge and memory; Rust retains execution authority. Native training and human-controlled promotion form a separate planned loop. Scoped implemented foundations do not establish integrated model, RAG or training acceptance.

steps.name: Compose
steps.title: Define a job, then compose its flow.
steps.text: Declare goals, authority, budgets, typed tools and reusable skills. Choose only the roles the job needs; nine roles do not mean nine mandatory models. Start with local text and source-grounded reporting; audio, vision and world models are optional.

steps.name: Assign
steps.title: Accept profiles, not model names.
steps.text: Match exact artifacts, operators, rights, schemas and hardware. Reasoning, planning, decision, action policy and retrieval remain distinct roles; speech input and output use separate profiles. Model manifests are implemented, but local inference remains explicitly unsupported until accepted.

steps.name: Inspect
steps.title: Ground context. Inspect actual effects.
steps.text: Retrieve only currently permitted project sources. The implemented memory adapter resolves explicit references; vector search, graph traversal and analytical engines remain separate gates. Native decision evidence links submitted alternatives to actual bounded tool outcomes; a prediction or graph link is not a verified fact.

steps.name: Improve
steps.title: Improve without widening permissions.
steps.text: Execution, collection, training, external disclosure and ecosystem export have separate rights. Derived data keeps source restrictions and lineage. Per-model native Rust gradients and LoRA/QLoRA are planned; external reference recipes do not prove owned-runtime training. Evaluate held-out tasks before controlled promotion.

concept_note: Architecture v0.7 · scoped components exist; integrated model jobs remain unaccepted
human_text: Define authority. Inspect observed outcomes. Keep stop and revocation on the Rust control path.
faq_intro: How the ecosystem fits together, what the subscriptions are intended to cover and what is still in development.

questions.question: What is Eyleme?
questions.answer: Eyleme is the shared brand and an independently usable open-source local task tool, with the ambition to grow into a community ecosystem. Derleme covers physical-world data collection and cloud or on-premises recording; Onama covers cybersecurity, authority, responsibility and regulatory workflows. The family is in development. First-party Eyleme core code and docs use Apache-2.0; Derleme and Onama are private-source products with planned paid subscriptions.

questions.question: Do I need a subscription to use Eyleme?
questions.answer: No. The open-source Eyleme tool can be used independently, with its own permission checks. Paid Derleme and Onama subscriptions are intended for specialist field-data and governance needs. Packages, prices, service levels and launch availability have not been published, and this site has no subscription checkout.

questions.question: Where will Derleme record field data?
questions.answer: The planned deployment options are cloud and on premises, within the customer’s own infrastructure. Derleme is intended to collect physical-world data with its source, timing and quality context. The actual connectors, storage setup and supported environment must be defined and accepted for each deployment. This is a product direction, not a claim that a customer installation is already available.

questions.question: What does Onama cover?
questions.answer: Onama focuses on cybersecurity, authorization, responsibility and regulatory compliance workflows: who may access data or act, under which policy, and how decisions and effects can be audited. It is a specialist product in development. Applicable requirements depend on the organization and deployment; the product does not itself provide legal certification or guarantee compliance. Eyleme’s basic local permission checks remain in the open-source core.

questions.question: What works today?
questions.answer: The core includes the task console and scoped native loop/model contracts, project-data gates, explicit-reference memory context, typed counter tools, reusable counter skills and decision evidence. Each component has its own proof and limits. This promotional site does not run them, and those proofs do not establish general inference, graph search or complete harness jobs.

questions.question: Has real human authorization been demonstrated?
questions.answer: Yes, in a bounded native macOS counter demonstration: an actual device-owner check, exact approval, effective stop before the remaining action, revocation and state-preserving reopen passed on 14 October 2026. This grants no data-training or sharing rights. The separate start --human/browser flow, remote identity and arbitrary model jobs were not part of that acceptance.

questions.question: Does every job need nine models?
questions.answer: No. The optional roles are perception, reasoning, planning, decision, action policy, world model, specialist, critic and representation/retrieval. One model may fill several compatible roles. Audio, vision and text profiles are distinct, and exact model acceptance is required before execution.

questions.question: Can I run local models or connect an external one now?
questions.answer: Declared model artifact and role contracts are implemented; they do not load weights or run inference. Local assignments still report unsupported execution. The architecture permits explicitly configured external frontier models, but configuration is not authorization to disclose private data or make paid calls. A local-only profile never silently falls back to a hosted model.

questions.question: How do RAG, memory and the knowledge graph fit?
questions.answer: The design grounds answers in permitted project documents and optional working, episodic, semantic, procedural, knowledge-graph and analytical memory. The current Rust adapter builds bounded context from explicit source references, rechecking rights, expiry and lineage. Semantic/vector retrieval, graph traversal, analytical engines and tokenizer counting remain separate acceptance gates.
questions.link: Implemented source context and memory limits

questions.question: How are decisions explained?
questions.answer: Native decision evidence joins submitted alternatives, constraints and declared model pins to actual scoped tool receipts and complete, partial or unknown outcomes. Confidence and model declarations remain unverified inputs. The current proof uses deterministic counter tools; model explanations, causal claims and whole-loop performance require separate evidence.

questions.question: Can private project data train or enter the ecosystem?
questions.answer: Not automatically. Execute, collect, train, external disclosure and ecosystem export are independent purposes. Derived records inherit current source restrictions; withdrawal blocks future use but does not erase published copies or unlearn weights. Ecosystem packages need explicit selection, provenance, terms, review and compatible import acceptance.

questions.question: How will local learning work?
questions.answer: The plan accepts training per exact model: owned Rust gradients, CPU/Metal LoRA and separately supported QLoRA, followed by independent evaluation and controlled promotion. Unsloth-like tooling remains a reviewed reference or recipe aid with separate export/reacceptance gates. No accepted native training or improved-model result is claimed.

questions.question: Which platform comes first?
questions.answer: The first experimental target is a single-user loopback application on a MacBook Pro with Apple M4 Pro and 24 GB unified memory. Browser and native execution have distinct boundaries. Mac mini M4 and Linux RTX equipment are additional inventory, not accepted support; remote access and Linux acceptance are future scope.

questions.question: What is the project license?
questions.answer: Eyleme first-party core code and documentation use Apache-2.0. Separately identified third-party material, model weights and datasets retain their own terms. This does not grant a blanket license to every asset or model, or change the website repository license.

foundation_cards.label: Implemented foundation
foundation_cards.title: A growing local Rust core.
foundation_cards.text: Task console, durable recovery, loop/model contracts, purpose-gated project data and bounded source context. Native tools, skill packages and decision evidence have scoped counter proofs; these are not general model or RAG execution.

foundation_cards.label: Architecture v0.7 · integration in development
foundation_cards.title: Compose a system for the job.
foundation_cards.text: Nine optional model roles, reusable skills, RAG and project memory. Local inference, native Rust training and complete jobs need their own acceptance. External models require explicit configuration and disclosure permission; local-only has no hosted fallback.

products_intro: Derleme → Onama → Eyleme: collect and record field data, govern access and responsibility, turn permitted inputs into action. These are complementary roles; authority checks apply throughout the workflow.

products.name: Eyleme Derleme
products.title: Bring the field into the record.
products.text: Derleme is being built to collect data from sensors, machines and field operations in the physical world, then record it in the cloud or on premises. Source, time and quality context support permitted downstream use. Each connector and deployment needs its own acceptance.
products.status: In development · subscription terms not yet published

products.name: Eyleme Onama
products.title: Define security and responsibility.
products.text: Onama is being built around cybersecurity, access authority, responsibilities, audit records and regulatory compliance workflows. It aims to make who may do what, under which rules and with whose responsibility explicit.
products.status: In development · subscription terms not yet published

products.name: Eyleme
products.title: Turn intent into action, together.
products.text: An open-source local task tool and the starting point for a community ecosystem. Public code, documentation, examples and reusable skills support its growth. The local foundation exists; the broader agentic platform is in development.
products.status: Public foundation · broader platform in development

products_note: Derleme and Onama extend the family without being required to use Eyleme. No paid checkout or production subscription service is available on this site. Pricing and availability will be published when ready.

subscriptions_intro: The commercial focus is Derleme and Onama: specialist products for bringing physical-world data into reliable records and defining how it may be accessed and used.

subscription_cards.label: Eyleme community
subscription_cards.title: No subscription required.
subscription_cards.text: Use the open-source local foundation, inspect its code and contribute to the ecosystem. First-party core code and documentation use Apache-2.0. Derleme and Onama subscriptions are optional.

subscription_cards.label: Derleme & Onama
subscription_cards.title: Paid specialist products.
subscription_cards.text: Derleme focuses on field integration, data quality and cloud or on-premises recording. Onama focuses on cybersecurity, authorization, responsibility and regulatory compliance workflows. These are the expertise areas behind the planned private-source subscriptions.
